correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Selected western head and North Canyon approach
correspondence.finding: The selected western beginning lies in the Baxter Spring/North Canyon setting beside the Highway 120 corridor. It runs east along the mapped North Canyon Creek corridor toward the Adobe Creek and Indian Meadow setting. The mapped Adobe Creek approaches from the south and continues into Adobe Valley. This is separate from the natural upper Owens River and Lake Crowley corridor visible farther southwest.
correspondence.correspondence: Original cartographic geography observed throughout this selected interval; no source-coverage gap asserted.
correspondence.name_scope: These names are bounded local channels. The selected beginning is not asserted to be either river’s exact official source.

correspondence.component_scope: Adobe Creek entry and northward Adobe Valley floor
correspondence.finding: After the canyon outlet, the selected line proceeds north across the broad Adobe Valley floor toward Adobe Lake. The original shows Adobe Creek and drainage/ditch traces on the western floor, with extensive intervening open valley terrain. The complete selected interval is observable, but it is not depicted as one continuously named river.
correspondence.correspondence: Original cartographic geography observed throughout this selected interval; no source-coverage gap asserted.
correspondence.name_scope: Adobe Lake is the cartographic lake label. No alias with the separately listed Adobe Reservoir is assumed.

correspondence.component_scope: Adobe Lake, River Spring Lakes, Antelope Lake and Black Lake chain
correspondence.finding: The selected line visits Adobe Lake, then runs southeast across the valley’s marshy and lacustrine margin through the River Spring Lakes and Antelope Lake settings, and south along the Black Lake depression. The sources distinguish lakes, wetlands, intermittent tributaries and intervening ground. This observed chain is not treated as a single river or evidence of continuous through-flow.
correspondence.correspondence: Original cartographic geography observed throughout this selected interval; no source-coverage gap asserted.
correspondence.name_scope: Each label belongs to its depicted waterbody or wetland setting. Neither Owens River nor Adobe Creek is extended over the entire chain.

correspondence.component_scope: Black Lake–Benton Hot Springs intervening divide
correspondence.finding: At the south end of the Black Lake depression the selected route turns east across mapped raised terrain toward Benton Hot Springs, before entering the Blind Spring Valley wetland setting. The original depicts the western intermittent drainage and eastern springs/wetland separately, with intervening relief. The closed-basin context independently supports treating this as an observed non-through-channel transition, rather than an unseen connecting river.
correspondence.correspondence: Original cartographic geography observed throughout this selected interval; no source-coverage gap asserted.
correspondence.name_scope: No stream name or continuous natural surface connection is assigned across the divide. The cause of the modeled linkage is not inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: Blind Spring Valley, Benton and Spring Canyon Creek
correspondence.finding: The selected route follows the Blind Spring Valley lowland northeast toward Benton, then turns south into the separately labeled Spring Canyon Creek corridor. The map shows northern Hutchinson Creek and the Benton valley setting independently. Those neighboring labels are not propagated upstream across the divide.
correspondence.correspondence: Original cartographic geography observed throughout this selected interval; no source-coverage gap asserted.
correspondence.name_scope: The selected wetland approach and the named creek are distinct components. Hutchinson Creek is contextual, not the selected head.

correspondence.component_scope: Hammil Valley and southward Spring Canyon Creek corridor
correspondence.finding: South of Benton, the selected route follows the Spring Canyon Creek corridor along the western side of the Highway 6 valley, past the Marble, Pellisier/Birch and Lone Tree tributary settings, then into the southward Chalfant wash terrain. Tributary names and irrigation traces remain separate.
correspondence.correspondence: Original cartographic geography observed throughout this selected interval; no source-coverage gap asserted.
correspondence.name_scope: Spring Canyon Creek is supported locally where labeled. No unsupported scalar extension across the entire Tri-Valley route is made.

correspondence.component_scope: Chalfant wash, McNally canals and Laws/Owens junction setting
correspondence.finding: The selected lower Tri-Valley line follows the mapped intermittent wash east of Fish Slough into the McNally canal and wetland country near Laws, then joins the Owens River corridor. The source shows the whole wash/canal/wetland transition. Fish Slough is a distinct western channel; the selected path is not renamed after it.
correspondence.correspondence: Original cartographic geography observed throughout this selected interval; no source-coverage gap asserted.
correspondence.name_scope: The unnamed selected wash remains unnamed. The county’s exceptional Chalfant–Laws surface-flow description supports an episodic connection, not a perennial river or a whole-route hydronym.

correspondence.component_scope: Owens River from Laws and Bishop to Big Pine
correspondence.finding: From the Laws junction setting the selection runs south and southeast with the mapped Owens River east of Bishop and past Big Pine. The original distinguishes North Fork Bishop Creek, local canals and other tributaries from the named river corridor.
correspondence.correspondence: Original cartographic geography observed throughout this selected interval; no source-coverage gap asserted.
correspondence.name_scope: Owens River is supported as the bounded middle/lower channel identity only. It is not a representative name for the entire selected composite.

correspondence.component_scope: Tinemaha Reservoir passage and Owens outlet reach
correspondence.finding: The selection enters the Tinemaha Reservoir river reach, traverses its western part at generalized corridor scale, and continues into the mapped Owens River below the impoundment. The reservoir and Tinemaha Creek are separately labeled. The lower view also distinguishes the Los Angeles Aqueduct diversion from the selected Owens River route.
correspondence.correspondence: Original cartographic geography observed throughout this selected interval; no source-coverage gap asserted.
correspondence.name_scope: The reservoir passage is not assigned a uniform river scalar name; exact shoreline or dam-point coincidence is not required.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Owens River from Aberdeen through Independence and Lone Pine
correspondence.finding: The selection continues in the Owens River corridor past the Aberdeen, Independence, Manzanar and Lone Pine settings. Original maps show the Los Angeles Aqueduct to the west and other canals/ditches separately. The selected line remains with the river corridor to its delta at the north side of Owens Lake.
correspondence.correspondence: Original cartographic geography observed throughout this selected interval; no source-coverage gap asserted.
correspondence.name_scope: The named lower-river component is supported. The independent project prose supplies bounded corridor context only.

correspondence.component_scope: Owens Lake delta and actual selected dry-bed terminal
correspondence.finding: Below the lower river and delta approach, the selection continues across the mapped Owens Lake bed, including a subdivided water/pond area, and ends farther into the area explicitly labeled Owens Lake (Dry). The final modeled extension is distinct from the mapped river/delta channel. The actual selected endpoint lies in this named dry-lake basin, not at a separately proven river mouth.
correspondence.correspondence: Original cartographic geography observed throughout this selected interval; no source-coverage gap asserted.
correspondence.name_scope: Owens Lake is independently observed terminal geography. The final lake-bed extension is not named Owens River; no modern water extent, exact mouth, or flow condition is established.

correspondence.component_scope: Headward Turimiquire and El Guamo setting
correspondence.finding: The original 2012 Costa oriental sheet maps El Guamo in the mountainous northern part of the drainage and a connected channel continuing south. Its small-scale representation does not resolve the full selected headward branch or reservoir passage. The chapter's Miraflores Guarapiche photograph caption is location context, not a mapped connector.

correspondence.finding: PROVEA's original map 2 places a labeled Río Guarapiche along the eastward river corridor south of Jusepín and toward Maturín. correspondence.finding: Sheet 55 depicts the southward drainage below El Guamo curving east and northeast into the river network labeled Guarapiche, with an onward junction into Río San Juan. correspondence.finding: The selected northern component occupies the Epenche valley west of Mazamitla, near Epenche Grande. It is not named Coahuayana throughout, and the study’s generalized Cerro del Tigre origin is not substituted for this selected head.

correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.finding: Instead of remaining on that westward channel, the selected course extends south across the mapped Mesa de Mota interfluve toward the headward Agua Zarca drainage, then returns northwest along the valley labelled El Tejocote on the finer SGM sheets.
